Dynamical Spanning Tree Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch56.R
centrality_dst.Rd

Dynamical spanning tree (DST) centrality (Chen et al. 2003, as given by Lu et al. 2016) is the share of the spanning trees of a network that is lost when a node is removed: $$DST(i) = 1 - \frac{t(G \setminus \{v_i\})}{t(G)},$$ where \(t\) counts spanning trees.

Usage

centrality_dst(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order, between 0 and 1, or NA at every node when the network is disconnected.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The counts come from the matrix-tree theorem. A node whose removal disconnects the network scores 1, and a node with one neighbor scores 0. On a disconnected network and on a single node every score is NA with a cograph_undefined_measure warning. The definition follows equation (50) of Lu et al. (2016); the 2003 paper was not consulted. The measure is different from the spanning_tree measure of centrality. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Chen, Y., Hu, A.-Q., Yip, K.-W., Hu, J. and Zhong, Z.-G. (2003). Finding the most vital node with respect to the number of spanning trees. In Proceedings of the 2003 International Conference on Neural Networks and Signal Processing, 2, 1670-1673. doi:10.1109/ICNNSP.2003.1281204 .

Lu, L., Chen, D., Ren, X.-L., Zhang, Q.-M., Zhang, Y.-C. and Zhou, T. (2016). Vital nodes identification in complex networks. Physics Reports, 650, 1-63. doi:10.1016/j.physrep.2016.06.007 .

See also

centrality_mec, centrality.

Examples

centrality_dst(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.9105337  0.9425221  0.9592007  0.9455253  0.9185185  0.9086591  0.8545165 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.9028054  0.9384110  0.9019912
